title: Forgive My Heart Its Vain Regrets
description: Forgive My Heart Its Vain Regrets in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: For-give my heart its vain re-grets, And, as I cast my eyes be-hind, Sub-due the spir-it, Lord, that frets, Be-cause the light with dark is twined.

lines: Forgive my heart its vain regrets,
And, as I cast my eyes behind,
Subdue the spirit, Lord, that frets,
Because the light with dark is twined.
I cannot understand the way
By which unerring wisdom leads;
Nor do I know for what to pray,
Unconscious of my deepest needs.
Thou, Whose almighty power upholds
The stars that in their courses move, —
Whose eye creation's need beholds
To prompt the outflow of Thy love; —
Teach me in calm content to live
'Mid all the changes life contains,
Assured that, love and wisdom give
The blessing that for aye remains.
And in the darkness and the light,
And in the gladness and the pain,
Make me to know that all is right,
And every loss my truest gain.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
